root_idea.summary: The attested lexical nucleus is تِينٌ, the familiar fig; the same noun is also reported for a mountain in an alternative interpretation of the Quranic oath.
root_idea.development: The supplied root analysis treats تِينٌ as an isolated lexical item rather than establishing a broader abstract root principle. Classical usage extends it from the fig as tree or fruit to named varieties, fig gardens, and related trade terms.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The supplied QAC group is a Quran-attested nominal for تِينٌ and is best displayed under the normalized classical citation form تِينٌ.

senses.definition: The fig: the fig tree, its edible fruit, or both.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic oath at 95:1, the ordinary interpretation takes تِينٌ as the familiar fig, with the referent understood as the tree, the fruit, or both.

senses.definition: A mountain, in an alternative interpretation of the Quranic oath.
senses.usage_conditions: At 95:1, the paired terms تِين and زَيْتُون are also interpreted as two mountains or associated sacred places rather than the edible fruits. Reported identifications include locations in Syria or the Holy Land, but no single geographic identification is established here.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A named variety of fig, including the sycamore or Egyptian fig and, in later appellations, the Indian fig or prickly pear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are varietal or naming extensions of the fig noun, not separate Quranic senses.
An anatomical use of the feminine derivative تِينَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fig-garden; land abounding in figs.
To deviate from or miss the right way, lose one’s way, become perplexed, or be unable to see the right course; in an attested extension, to perish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is also used of a ship deviating from its course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the eye or sight, to pass over or fail to notice someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction with sight as the subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To look at something continually or continuously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported specialized use of the sight-related construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To magnify oneself; behave proudly, haughtily, insolently, conceitedly, or vaingloriously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a distinct personal-behavior use of the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone or something lose the way or become perplexed; reflexively, to bring oneself into confusion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form II use, including the reflexive construction تَيَّهَ نَفْسَهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To destroy, lose, abandon, or neglect someone or something; reflexively, to destroy oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A further causative or resultative use of the Form II verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A desert or land without landmarks in which one loses the way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can designate a broad, signless wilderness; specifically, it is also used for the wilderness in which the Children of Israel were said to have lost their way.
An adjective applied in the cited usage to a man or a camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pursuing a random or heedless course without a definite aim or object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man or camel; the feminine form is used for a she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Deviating from or losing the right way; becoming perplexed and unable to see the correct course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The use may be figurative of a person desiring something but unable to find the right course in opinion or judgment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Proud, haughty, insolent, conceited, or vainglorious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can describe one who claims praise for qualities or accomplishments he does not possess; related intensive forms are also recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The most proud or conceited of people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported superlative expression; the supplied evidence presents this interpretation tentatively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man characterized by excessive pride, conceit, or vanity, or by frequently losing the way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional noun combining the intensive personal and wandering uses of تِيه.

cautions: The mountain reading is an alternative interpretation of Quran 95:1, and the supplied evidence does not establish one modern geographic identification.

The supplied Lane primary set includes separately headed forms such as تَاهَ and تِيهٌ alongside تِينٌ. They have been retained under their own headwords rather than conflated with the Quranic noun; the packet does not independently explain the relation of those headed forms to the canonical QAC root.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The packet supplies Lane entries headed تَاهَ, تِيهٌ, and related derivatives within the primary context for تين, but provides no independent root-linkage explanation for that grouping. Their lexical content is represented under their supplied headwords, while the grouping itself remains unresolved.
